summary: Jordan issues most nationalities a single-entry visa on arrival for JOD 40 allowing a 30-day stay, and waives that fee entirely for travelers who buy the Jordan Pass (which bundles Petra and 40+ sites) and stay at least two nights (3 days), according to the official Jordan Pass site — while about 50 nationalities, most of them African and Asian, need prior approval from the Ministry of Interior or an embassy visa.

conditionalWaivers.text: Ordinary-passport holders who live in a GCC country — or in the US, Canada, Australia, Japan, South Korea, the EU, the Nordic countries or the UK — can get a visa on arrival without the Ministry of Interior's prior approval, provided their residence permit is valid for at least 6 more months; arrivals by air must also hold a return ticket. The same applies to holders of a Schengen or US visa valid for at least 6 months. Nationals of Nigeria, Iran and Bangladesh, and holders of travel documents, still need prior approval.

source.name: Jordan Ministry of Interior — FAQ (entry of residents of foreign countries; nationalities needing prior approval)

fee.notes: Payable in Jordanian dinars (cards accepted at Amman airport). Double-entry (JOD 60) and multiple-entry (JOD 120) visas are available from embassies. The official Jordan Pass site says the fee is waived if you buy the pass before arrival and stay at least two nights (3 days); the UK Foreign Office gives the minimum as 3 nights. The fee is also waived for travelers arriving via Aqaba's special economic zone.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Jordan entry requirements

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on the date of arrival in Jordan.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Jordan entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement. Medical facilities outside Amman and Aqaba are basic, so cover for treatment and medical evacuation is strongly recommended.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Jordan entry requirements

onwardTicket.text: No official Jordanian source we could read states a general onward-ticket rule for visitors. The Ministry of Interior requires a return ticket only from air arrivals who get a visa on arrival on the strength of a foreign residence permit; airlines may still ask other travelers.

source.name: Jordan Ministry of Interior — FAQ (entry of residents of foreign countries; nationalities needing prior approval)

proofOfFunds.text: No official Jordanian source we could read states a proof-of-funds requirement or amount for visitors.

source.name: Visit Jordan — entry requirements

currencyLimits.text: Cash and bearer negotiable instruments worth more than JOD 10,000 in total (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared to Customs on arrival and on departure.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says you must apply for approval to bring a drone into Jordan at least 10 working days before travel; without a permit the authorities hold the drone at the airport and you collect it when you leave.
Canada's travel advice says penalties for illegal drugs are severe: even small amounts are a criminal offence, and you could be held for up to 2 weeks without charge.

payments.text: The UK Foreign Office says most places accept card payments but cash machines are widely available only in Amman and other major towns. Canada's travel advice says larger stores and restaurants in Amman and tourist areas accept credit cards, ATMs are limited outside the larger cities and Queen Alia airport, and only US dollars and euros are easily converted into dinars.

safety.text: Tourist areas are generally calm, but the FCDO reports Iranian strikes in Jordan since 8 July 2026, with renewed attacks and interceptions in and around Aqaba in early September, and warns of short-notice airspace closures. It advises against all travel within 3 km of the Syrian border. Stay away from military sites and strategic infrastructure, and follow local instructions to shelter.

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Jordan. Canada's travel advice says the rainy season usually runs from November to March, with a risk of flash floods in wadis and on roads, and that snowfall is infrequent but can close roads.

idp.text: Jordan is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: The Ministry of Tourism's Jordan Pass site sells three passes, from 70 to 80 JD, with one to three days at Petra and free entry to over 40 attractions; the tourist visa fee is waived if you buy the pass before arrival and stay at least two nights (3 days). The UK Foreign Office gives the minimum as 3 nights. Buy only from jordanpass.jo.
At the Dead Sea, float on your back and keep the water away from your eyes and any cuts — shower promptly afterward, and bring flip-flops as the salt crystals are sharp.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Jordan?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is issued on arrival: a single-entry visa costs JOD 40 (about USD 56) and allows a 30-day stay, which the Ministry of Interior can extend for up to 6 months from the date of entry. The Ministry of Tourism's Jordan Pass site says the visa fee is waived if you buy the pass before arrival and stay at least two nights (3 days).

faq.question: Is the Jordan Pass worth it?
faq.answer: It depends on your plans. The Ministry of Tourism's Jordan Pass site sells three passes — 70 JD (one day at Petra), 75 JD (two days) and 80 JD (three days) — each with free entry to over 40 attractions, and the tourist visa fee is waived if you buy it before arrival and stay at least two nights (3 days). Buy it only at jordanpass.jo.

faq.question: How do I pay for the Jordan visa on arrival?
faq.answer: The JOD 40 fee is charged in Jordanian dinars. At Queen Alia International Airport you can pay by card or exchange money before the immigration counters; at land borders bring cash. Jordan Pass holders skip payment and simply show the pass QR code.

faq.question: Can I stay in Jordan longer than 30 days?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply to extend before your initial 30 days expire — online through the Ministry of Interior's e-services, or at a local police station — and your stay can be extended for up to 6 months from the date you entered, without leaving the country. Overstaying without an extension incurs a fine of JOD 1.5 per day at departure.

faq.question: Can Indian citizens get a visa on arrival in Jordan?
faq.answer: Generally yes — Indian passport holders have been able to obtain the JOD 40 visa on arrival, but conditions for Indian, Filipino, Indonesian and Vietnamese nationals have changed several times (group-travel or prior-approval requirements have applied in some periods). Confirm the current rule with a Jordanian embassy or your airline before booking.
